title: Convert to PLINK 2 native format

blocks.what_we_do: Convert the matched BED/BIM/FAM export to PGEN/PVAR/PSAM.
blocks.why: PGEN stores genotypes, PVAR describes sites and PSAM describes samples. These are PLINK 2 native files. BED/BIM/FAM remain useful for older tools, but neither format determines the genome build. Binary conversion must preserve sample and variant identity and order.
blocks.you_need: The original matched files checked at 2.1.
blocks.command:
```{r s2-2}
out <- guided_path(cfg, "2.2")
run_plink(cfg, c("--bfile", cfg$input, "--make-pgen", "--out", out), paste0(out, c(".pgen", ".pvar", ".psam")))
stopifnot(all(guided_counts(out) == c(2016, 299523)))
guided_source_checkpoint(cfg)
```

Plain PLINK 2 command (use `bin\plink2.exe` on Windows):

```sh
bin/plink2 --bfile data/course/lab_export/sim2026_lab --make-pgen --out results/guided/s2-2_state --threads 2 --memory 2048
```

`--bfile` takes the common prefix of the BED/BIM/FAM set. `--make-pgen` writes a new native fileset. `--out` sets the output prefix; `--threads 2` and `--memory 2048` bound resources. The R helper prints the exact command with your own safe paths.
blocks.expected_result:
2,016 samples and 299,523 variants are preserved. An imported BED does not establish the genomic reference allele: PLINK can mark REF as provisional.

The tested PLINK version is defined in `config.R` and recorded in
`software_versions.txt`. Validation: executable chunks and available instructor reference counts passed on Windows.
blocks.troubleshooting: Stop at the first error. Check the named input and the previous step. Keep the command and console logs; do not substitute files from a different dataset version. See [troubleshooting](../docs/troubleshooting.md).
blocks.quick_check:
Does converting BED to PGEN automatically convert GRCh37 coordinates to GRCh38?

<details><summary>Show the answer</summary>

No. Storage format and genome assembly are separate properties.

</details>
blocks.files_created: `s2-2_state.pgen/.pvar/.psam`, command and console logs under the output folder.
